name: Pinoline
summary: Pinoline, also known as 6-methoxytryptoline or as 6-methoxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-β-carboline (6-MeO-THβC), is a β-carboline long-claimed to be produced in the pineal gland during the metabolism of melatonin, however its pineal occurrence remains controversial. Its more common name is a contraction of "pineal β-carboline".

pharmacology.text: Pinoline shows affinity for serotonin receptors, including the serotonin 5-HT1A, 5-HT2A, 5-HT2B, 5-HT2C, and 5-HT7 receptors (Ki = 156–4,335 nM).

uses.text: It remains unknown whether pinoline has hallucinogenic effects in humans.

fact.en: Pinoline is a close chemical cousin of the harmala alkaloids found in Syrian rue. Like them, it can block the enzyme monoamine oxidase A in laboratory tests.
fact.zh: Pinoline 和駱駝蓬中的哈爾馬生物鹼是化學上的近親。和它們一樣，它在實驗室測試中能抑制單胺氧化酶 A。
